req.title: Index renders even with zero posts
req.statement: The system shall render the index page with 'No posts' or empty state when the post table is empty.
triggers: index renders even with zero posts

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-037 requires the index page (GET /) to render successfully with HTTP 2xx even when the post table is empty. Three tests are designed: (1) positive — empty DB, verify 200 and page renders without crashing; (2) negative — verify that with posts present the page still returns 200 but contains post content (distinguishing empty vs non-empty state, catching mutations that invert the empty-check logic); (3) boundary — exactly zero posts (the boundary value), asserting the response body does NOT contain any known post title from the seeded data, confirming the empty-state branch is taken. All tests use exact status code assertions and content checks to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_index_empty_db_returns_200
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh empty database (init_db called, no posts inserted)
expected: Response does not contain any seeded post title
trace: R-FLASKR-037: index renders even with zero posts -> HTTP 2xx response
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    # post table is now empty (no rows inserted)
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert len(r.data) > 0
# None of the seeded post titles should appear
assert b'Pulse ember signal' not in r.data
assert b'Pillow delta willow' not in r.data
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' not in r.data
os.unlink(path)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute("INSERT INTO user (id, username, password) VALUES (1, 'Rahul', 'x')")
    db.execute("INSERT INTO post (id, author_id, title, body, created) VALUES (20, 1, 'Heacon signal pulse', 'body text', '2025-04-01 10:30:37')")
    db.commit()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data
assert len(r.data) > 0
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_index_exactly_zero_posts_boundary
preconditions: Database schema is initialised via init_db()
Post table contains exactly 0 rows (boundary value)
actions: Inspect status code and response body
expected: HTTP status code is exactly 200 (not 404, not 500)
Response body does not contain any seeded post title
Response body length is greater than 0 (page skeleton rendered)
trace: R-FLASKR-037: boundary at post count == 0; BVA catches off-by-one mutations in post-count checks; comparison-mutation on status code 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    count = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
    assert count == 0  # confirm boundary: exactly zero posts
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert r.status_code != 404
assert r.status_code != 500
assert len(r.data) > 0
# Confirm none of the 20 seeded titles appear (empty state)
for title in [b'Pulse ember signal', b'Pillow delta willow', b'Bmber matrix orbit',
              b'Nlpha quartz delta', b'Heacon signal pulse']:
    assert title not in r.data
os.unlink(path)
